name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Gary Palmer running with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: Palmer is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 17 points, while Maurice Mercer has raised only about $6,500. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican hold, so the baseline stands.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected incumbent scandal would be the main way this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gary Palmer, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in Alabama's 6th District, a seat that leans Republican by 17 points on the partisan vote index. He has raised over $1 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic nominee Maurice Mercer has raised under $7,000 and has essentially no cash on hand. No outside groups are opposing Palmer, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Palmer roughly a 95 percent chance of winning, and no general-election polling exists to suggest otherwise. With the incumbent renominated and the challenger lacking resources, the district's strong Republican lean makes this a safe Republican seat in all available evidence.
